cohort: The study included 17,621 assessments and 7877 scores from infants aged 0-1 year who visited a tertiary maternal and children hospital in eastern China for routine neurodevelopmental assessment.
finding: Infants assessed during the pandemic (stage II) had a higher risk of neurodevelopmental delay compared to pre-pandemic (stage I) and post-pandemic (stage III) infants, with stage III infants showing the highest risk of mental development delay.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as an independent risk factor for neurodevelopmental delay.
cross-section timing: January 2019 to July 2023, categorized into pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic stages.
